From cc57232cae23c0df91b4a59d0f519141ce9b5b02 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Shen <grayhat@foxmail.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 22:07:16 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] ksmbd: fix FSCTL permission bypass by adding a permission
 check for FSCTL_SET_SPARSE

FSCTL_SET_SPARSE in fsctl_set_sparse() modifies the file's sparse
attribute and saves it through xattr without any permission checks.

This exposes two issues:

1) A client on a read-only share can change the sparse attribute
   on files it opened, even though the share is read-only.
   Other FSCTL write operations already check
   test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE),
   but FSCTL_SET_SPARSE does not.

2) Even on writable shares, clients without FILE_WRITE_DATA or
   FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES access should not modify the sparse
   attribute. Similar handle-level checks exist in other functions
   but are missing here.

Add both share-level writable check and per-handle access check.
Use goto out on error to avoid leaking file references.

Fixes: e2f34481b24d ("cifsd: add server-side procedures for SMB3")
Cc: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>
Cc: Sergey Senozhatsky <sergey.senozhatsky@gmail.com>
Cc: Steve French <smfrench@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Sean Shen <grayhat@foxmail.com>
Acked-by: Namjae Jeon <linkinjeon@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <stfrench@microsoft.com>

diff --git a/fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c b/fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c
index 5128a693aca6..620bcfbbfd92 100644
--- a/fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c
+++ b/fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c
@@ -8202,9 +8202,20 @@ static inline int fsctl_set_sparse(struct ksmbd_work *work, u64 id,
 	int ret = 0;
 	__le32 old_fattr;
 
+	if (!test_tree_conn_flag(work->tcon, KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE)) {
+		ksmbd_debug(SMB, "User does not have write permission\n");
+		return -EACCES;
+	}
+
 	fp = ksmbd_lookup_fd_fast(work, id);
 	if (!fp)
 		return -ENOENT;
+
+	if (!(fp->daccess & (FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE | FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE))) {
+		ret = -EACCES;
+		goto out;
+	}
+
 	idmap = file_mnt_idmap(fp->filp);
 
 	old_fattr = fp->f_ci->m_fattr;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c` to fix a permission bypass vulnerability in the `fsctl_set_sparse` function. Two security checks are added: a share-level writability check and a per-handle access rights check. Additionally, error handling is improved by using `goto out` to ensure proper cleanup on failure.

**Modifications in each file:**

- **`fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c`**:  
  - Added a check for `KSMBD_TREE_CONN_FLAG_WRITABLE` on the tree connection. If the share is read-only, the function now returns `-EACCES` immediately.  
  - After obtaining the file pointer (`fp`), a check is performed on `fp->daccess` to require either `FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE` or `FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES_LE` access. If neither is granted, the function sets `ret = -EACCES` and jumps to the existing `out` label to avoid modifying the sparse attribute.  

**Relationships between the modifications:**

- Both checks are within the same function `fsctl_set_sparse`, forming a layered access control: the share-level check prevents modifications on read-only shares, while the per-handle check restricts changes to clients with appropriate write permissions.  
- The `goto out` on permission failure ensures the function returns early without executing the attribute-modification logic, preventing resource leaks (since the file pointer remains valid but is not used further).  
- Together, these changes address two distinct issues (read-only share bypass and insufficient handle-level checks) with a unified error-handling pattern.
